description: The chair of a law firm's technology-transactions group must approve an exclusive patent license for a biotechnology client and finalize the licensed field, economics, government-use protections, and conflicts safeguards before execution.

shared_context.S1: The firm represents a biotechnology company licensing a patent portfolio to a diagnostics company.
shared_context.S2: The proposed agreement grants the counterparty an exclusive commercial license and is scheduled for execution next week.
shared_context.S3: The current draft grants worldwide exclusivity, sets a royalty rate of 3% of net sales, and contains no annual royalty minimum.
shared_context.S4: Under the firm's routine pre-execution review, Elena asks patent, client-relationship, finance, and conflicts counsel to report any issue that should change the final agreement.

PF1.text: Noah confirmed by reviewing the patent prosecution and grant records that one licensed invention received federal funding; the agreement must reserve U.S. government-use rights and require the licensee to maintain U.S. manufacturing for covered products. He has not yet added those requirements to the draft comments.

PF2.text: Maya confirmed with the client this week that the client will grant exclusivity only for oncology diagnostics and must retain a non-exclusive right to use the technology for its own internal research; those business instructions have not yet been circulated to the drafting team.

PF3.text: Thomas checked three comparable biotechnology licenses and confirmed that the client's approved economics are a 4.5% royalty on net sales plus a $300,000 annual minimum royalty; he has not entered the benchmark into the transaction summary.

PF4.text: Sofia found in the firm's conflicts database that the counterparty's founder is a current firm client in an unrelated matter adverse to the licensing client; execution requires the founder's informed written consent and an ethical screen for the unrelated matter, neither of which has been documented.

acceptance_conditions: Execution may be approved only with exclusivity limited to oncology diagnostics.
The biotechnology company must retain a non-exclusive internal research right.
The royalty rate must be exactly 4.5% of net sales.
The agreement must require exactly a $300,000 annual minimum royalty.
The agreement must reserve U.S. government-use rights.
The agreement must require U.S. manufacturing for covered products.
The conflict must be resolved through informed written consent before execution.
An ethical screen must be established for the unrelated matter.
The final agreement must include commitments implementing the government-use and U.S.-manufacturing requirements.

content_checks.C9: any(c['type'] == 'government_use_reservation' for c in commitments) and any(c['type'] == 'us_manufacturing' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The federal-funding confirmation changes the draft from having no special public-rights terms to reserving U.S. government use and requiring U.S. manufacturing, with two matching commitments.
The client's instruction changes worldwide exclusivity to oncology-diagnostics-only exclusivity and adds the company's specific non-exclusive internal research right.
The comparable-license review changes the economics from the draft's 3% royalty with no minimum to exactly 4.5% and a $300,000 annual minimum royalty.

The conflicts finding changes an apparently executable agreement into one requiring the founder's informed written consent and an ethical screen, and it supplies the conflict fact that must be cited by the decision-maker.
